metadata.notes: Smallest clean compile in the test set (112-line spec). One-shot reasoning with public HTTP tool (wttr.in). Demonstrates the minimal D1 / One-shot pattern: single input slot, single output, no nested compositions. Use as worked example for request-response skills where the pipeline is a straight call-and-return.

notes: D1/P2 thin wrapper around wttr.in HTTP API.
call_wttr is emitted as a stub in pipeline.py (returns empty string).
main.py patches pipeline.call_wttr with tools.call_wttr before invoking run_pipeline.
This pattern allows fixtures to run without network access (stub returns '') while production uses the real HTTP implementation.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: Natural language weather query including a location (e.g. 'What is the weather in London?' or 'Will it rain in Tokyo tomorrow?')

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Formatted weather response for the user

intent.description: Weather query intent: current_conditions, forecast_3day, forecast_week, forecast_day, precipitation, custom_format, or out_of_scope

location.description: City, region, or airport code for the weather query. Empty string if intent is out_of_scope.

response.description: Formatted weather response text for the user.

dependencies.rationale: HTTP tool calling wttr.in. Stub returns empty string so fixtures run offline. main.py replaces with tools.call_wttr via module-level patching before calling run_pipeline.

description.template: Parse this weather query. Set 'intent' to one of: [current_conditions, forecast_3day, forecast_week, forecast_day, precipitation, custom_format, out_of_scope]. Set 'location' to the city, region, or airport code mentioned (empty string if intent is out_of_scope). Query: {query}

notes: Extracts weather intent and location from natural language query
Fetches weather data via call_wttr and formats the response using LLM
